modules.name: leave
owns: LeaveRequest entity (with state-transition rules: PENDING→APPROVED, PENDING→REJECTED, PENDING→CANCELLED)

modules.name: balance
owns: LeaveBalance entity (employeeId, leaveType, fiscalYear, totalDays, usedDays — computed remainingDays)

modules.name: policy
owns: LeavePolicy entity (leaveType, maxDaysPerYear, maxConsecutiveDays, requiresDocumentation, minNoticeHours, allowNegativeBalance)

modules.name: employee
owns: Employee entity (id, name, email, managerId, departmentId, role)

modules.name: notification
owns: NotificationService implementation (sends notifications on leave status changes)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Shared types and base infrastructure
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency foundation. Establish LeaveType, LeaveStatus enums and BaseEntity interface in src/shared/types/. Create the base repository pattern in src/shared/ if not already present. Every downstream module depends on these.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Employee module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared-types. Provides employee lookup, manager hierarchy, and RBAC primitives. The leave module needs employee data for submitter/approver resolution.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared-types. Manages leave balances per employee/type/fiscal-year. The leave module calls balance checks and deductions during the approval workflow.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Policy module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared-types. Encodes leave policy rules (max days, notice periods, documentation requirements). The leave module validates requests against policy before submission.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5: Notification module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared-types. Provides notification dispatch on leave lifecycle events. The leave module calls notification methods after state transitions.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 6: Leave module (core orchestration)
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on employee, policy, balance, notification, and shared-types. Orchestrates the full leave workflow: validates against policy, checks balance, resolves manager, persists request, triggers notifications, and writes audit records. This is the integration hub.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: shared-types (innermost) → employee/policy/balance/notification (domain) → leave (application orchestration). The leave module is the only module that depends on other domain modules; it orchestrates the full workflow: validate policy → check balance → resolve manager → persist → notify → audit. All domain modules depend only on shared-types. No circular dependencies exist. Each module exposes its public API through an index.ts barrel file. Repositories follow GP-001; all state-changing operations write audit records per GP-002; RBAC is enforced at the route/controller layer per GP-005.

open_questions.question: How is remainingDays computed — stored as a derived column (totalDays - usedDays) in the DB, or computed at query time? If stored, what keeps it consistent with usedDays after every deduction/restore?
open_questions.impact: Affects Balance entity design, repository queries, and transaction isolation strategy in BalanceService.deductBalance and BalanceService.restoreBalance.
candidate_options: Stored computed column updated via DB trigger on usedDays changes
Computed at query time in the repository/SQL layer
Stored as a materialized field updated in the same transaction as usedDays

open_questions.question: What is the fiscal-year boundary rule? Is it calendar year (Jan 1–Dec 31), a configurable start month, or per-company? Does a leave spanning the boundary consume days from the start-date fiscal year, the end-date fiscal year, or split proportionally?
open_questions.impact: Affects BalanceService.deductBalance, BalanceService.getBalance, and the LeaveRequestService.submitLeaveRequest validation logic. The rule must be consistent across all balance operations.
candidate_options: Configurable fiscal year start month per tenant/company
Leave consumes days from the fiscal year of the start date
